description: WifiHaven PRESS/PR responder (#2203, epic #2197): the public press@wifihaven.net inbox handled by a Cloudflare Email Worker → /api/press/inbound → an Anthropic Managed Agents press session → the reply emailed straight back to the sender. Series: press_ai_draft_total{outcome,reason} (inbound-webhook outcomes — dispatched / rate_limited / invalid_signature / malformed / disabled / error), press_agent_action_total{op,outcome} (the press agent's reply callback — reply × ok / denied / rate_limited / disabled / error), and press_message_recorded_total{direction,outcome} (#2296 the correspondence-log audit writes — inbound|outbound × ok|error; fail-open, so error = a lost audit row while the webhook/reply still succeeded). All labels are bounded enums (never per-sender / per-thread). NO household data path (press is public); the recorded log is surfaced only to the household-1 admin. The responder runs iff the explicit press.responderEnabled flag is set (#2265 — no dark-by-default; a true flag with missing config, or with outbound email off, refuses to boot). #2438 adds press_dispatch_total{outcome,transport} — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome (dispatched / error / disabled) at the transport boundary, isolating a silent non-2xx trigger failure the inbound-webhook metric can't surface. See issues #2203, #2197, #2265, #2296, #2438. #2437 adds operator_escalation_total{channel="press",kind="escalated",outcome}: press has no inbox, so this is the ONLY channel by which an escalation reaches a human (#2480 dropped the per-inbound kind=received FYI — routine AI-handled traffic is monitored at /press, the #2296 correspondence log, not by email) — plus the press_agent_action_total op escalate.

panels.title: Inbound webhook outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(press_ai_draft_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — dispatched (a press cloud-agent session was created) / rate_limited (the per-sender + global dispatch cost caps fired) / invalid_signature (unsigned or forged POST — security-relevant, investigate a sustained rate; the Worker↔API HMAC is the only auth) / malformed (missing from/text) / skipped_auto_submitted (#2442 — the Cloudflare Worker classified the delivery as an auto-reply, mailing-list post or bounce, so no session was dispatched; the loop-guard panels below split that bucket by reason) / disabled (responder dark) / error (Managed Agents dispatch failed). Emitted by PressResponder.handleInbound.

panels.title: Agent callback actions
panels.description: sum by (op, outcome) (rate(press_agent_action_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatched press agent's token-authenticated reply callback: op=reply × ok (the reply was emailed to the sender — destination locked into the token) / denied (bad/expired/missing token — uniform 401) / disabled (responder dark) / error (Resend send failed). There is deliberately no issue-filing or household-read op (press is public — no data path). Emitted by PressResponder.agentReply.

panels.title: Press sessions dispatched (24h) — cost watch
panels.description: sum(increase(press_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="dispatched"}[24h])) — press cloud-agent sessions started in the last 24h. Each session bills API tokens (rough order: a few cents/reply on Sonnet 5); the global dispatch cap (50/day) bounds the ceiling. Red at the cap = sustained press-inbox spam or a Worker retry loop — check the rate_limited / invalid_signature outcomes on the webhook panel.

panels.title: Press replies emailed (24h)
panels.description: sum(increase(press_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="reply",outcome="ok"}[24h])) — replies the press agent emailed to journalists in the last 24h. Because replies send WITHOUT human review, spot-check early ones — the recipient is server-locked (the original sender) and the agent has no data access, so a prompt injection is bounded to a courteous-but-unhelpful public reply.

panels.title: Forged/unsigned inbound (24h) — security watch
panels.description: sum(increase(press_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="invalid_signature"}[24h])) — inbound POSTs to /api/press/inbound that failed HMAC verification in the last 24h. The Worker↔API signature is the only authentication on this public endpoint; a sustained non-zero rate means someone is probing it (harmless — rejected 400 before any dispatch), but a spike is worth a look.

panels.title: Correspondence recorded
panels.description: sum by (direction, outcome) (rate(press_message_recorded_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — #2296 the press correspondence log's best-effort AUDIT writes: direction=inbound|outbound × outcome=ok|error. Recording is FAIL-OPEN (a DB error never breaks the webhook or the reply), so an `error` series means the audit row was lost while the webhook/reply still succeeded — a rising error rate means the household-1 press log is silently drifting from reality. Emitted by PressResponder.recordInbound / recordOutbound.

panels.title: Outreach send outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(press_outreach_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — #2233 the operator-run press-OUTREACH send. One series per bounded outcome: sent / failed (Resend transport) / skipped_already_sent (idempotency) / skipped_no_email (form-only contact) / skipped_disabled (email off) / dry_run (preview or unconfirmed — never transmitted). Emitted by PressOutreachRoutes once per per-contact result. A `failed` series is a Resend delivery problem to investigate; `dry_run` reflects preview activity.

panels.title: Outreach emails sent (24h)
panels.description: sum(increase(press_outreach_total{env="$env",outcome="sent"}[24h])) — #2233 real press emails transmitted in the last 24h.

panels.title: Outreach sends failed (24h) — delivery watch
panels.description: sum(increase(press_outreach_total{env="$env",outcome="failed"}[24h])) — #2233 press emails Resend rejected in the last 24h. Non-zero = investigate the transport; a re-run retries failed contacts.

panels.title: Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes (#2438)
panels.description: sum by (outcome, transport) (rate(press_dispatch_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome, measured at the transport boundary (the SAME shared CloudAgentObservability envelope as support): dispatched (the Managed Agents session / Claude Code Cloud routine trigger returned 2xx) / error (the trigger returned non-2xx or the call threw — the press agent NEVER started, so no reply was emailed) / disabled (the responder is dark, #2265; carries no transport). transport ∈ managed-agents (API-credit billed) | claude-code-cloud (subscription billed). The 'Inbound webhook outcomes' panel's 'dispatched' only means a session was ATTEMPTED — a silent non-2xx trigger failure shows up as 'error' HERE and nowhere else. ALERT on any sustained 'error' rate while the responder is enabled (each is a journalist reply that never went out). #2416: when outcome=error, the 'Press dispatch failures by reason' panel below splits that bucket into config (a permanent 4xx misconfiguration — a dead responder needing a human fix, alert W7) vs transient (a 5xx/transport blip).

panels.title: Press dispatch failures by reason — dead-responder watch (#2416)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(press_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the press cloud agent could not be dispatched. Same bounded vocabulary as the support panel (one shared classifier, CloudAgentObservability), on the deliberately SEPARATE press series; complements the #2438 dispatch-outcomes panel by splitting its ERROR bucket by cause. config = a non-self-healing 4xx at the Anthropic boundary: a revoked/wrong press anthropicApiKey (401), a wrong press claudeAgentId / claudeEnvironmentId / claudeCodeRoutineId (404), or a STALE hard-coded anthropic-beta header (400) — NEVER self-heals, the press responder is dead until a human fixes the config; the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. transient = transport / timeout / 5xx, plus the 4xx that ARE load/timing signals (408, 429). ALERT on any sustained 'config' rate (warning rule W7). Journalists get NO reply while this is non-zero even though the inbound webhook still returns 200 (fail-open by design), so treat a config spike as customer-visible.

panels.title: Operator escalation notices, by delivery outcome (#2437)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="press"}[5m])) — #2437. Press has NO monitored inbox, so these emails to the operator are the ONLY way a handoff reaches a human; routine, AI-handled inquiries are read at /press (the #2296 correspondence log) and mail nobody. Every sample is the agent handing off because it cannot answer from public info or the sender wants a person: kind=escalated is the only value emitted since #2480 retired the per-inbound kind=received FYI, so THIS panel deliberately neither slices by kind nor pins it in the selector — any future kind would still be summed into these totals here (the 24h handoff panel beside it, and support.json's 5m + 24h twins, DO pin kind="escalated" and would need updating; the 24h outcome!="sent" panel does not). Any outcome other than `sent` means the operator was owed a notice and did not get it — for press that is a silently dropped journalist.

panels.title: Press escalations awaiting a human (24h) (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="press",kind="escalated"}[24h])) — press inquiries the agent handed off in the last 24h (interview requests, anything not answerable from public info). Each sender was told a team member would follow up, so this is a to-do count, not an error count.

panels.title: Press operator notices that never sent (24h) — expect 0 (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="press",outcome!="sent"}[24h])) — an escalation whose operator email did not go out (failed = Resend rejected it, skipped_disabled = the email transport is off, skipped_no_recipient = no wifihaven.email.operatorAddress). Press has no inbox to fall back on, so non-zero here means a journalist was dropped in silence.

panels.title: Agent callbacks REFUSED at the token check (#2473)
panels.description: sum by (op, reason) (rate(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="press"}[5m])) — Every sample is a cloud-agent callback we REFUSED at the token check — an answer that was generated and then thrown away at the door, so the customer/journalist received nothing. token_expired = a token WE minted outlived its TTL: the #2473 failure, where a claude-code-cloud run paused on subscription usage limits and resumed after the token had died. Sustained non-zero token_expired means agentTokenTtlMinutes is again shorter than the transport's real round-trip latency — raise it (api/src/Config.scala, AgentTokenTtl). invalid = malformed or wrongly-signed (a probe, or a secret rotation mid-flight); missing = no bearer at all. Both agent endpoints are public, so a low invalid/missing background rate is internet noise; token_expired never is.

panels.title: Press replies lost to an EXPIRED token (24h) — expect 0 (#2473)
panels.description: sum(increase(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="press",reason="token_expired"}[24h])) — each one is a journalist whose inquiry was answered and never delivered. Same cause and same fix as the support panel: the token outlived its TTL because the cloud-agent run paused on usage limits and resumed hours later.

panels.title: Live routine prompt version (#2469)
panels.description: sum by (state) (rate(agent_prompt_version_total{env="$env",channel="press"}[5m])) — what the LIVE cloud agent reports as its OWN prompt version on each reply callback, compared against the version compiled from deploy/press-agent/agent.yaml. current = the running agent matches this build. stale = it is answering journalists from an OLDER prompt: the Claude Code Cloud routine prompt is web-UI-only, so a merged prompt change stays inert until an operator re-pastes it at claude.ai/code/routines — and until they do, the routine reports a GREEN run while behaving from the old prompt (#2419/#2425 and #2430/#2441 both shipped that way). unknown = the agent reported no version at all, most likely a routine still on a pre-#2469 prompt. Alert-only: a mismatch never fails a webhook or drops a reply.

panels.title: Press replies from a DRIFTED routine (24h) — expect 0 (#2469)
panels.description: sum(increase(agent_prompt_version_total{env="$env",channel="press",state=~"stale|unknown"}[24h])) — each one is a journalist answered by a routine whose prompt does not match this build. The fix is manual and takes a minute: re-paste the system: block from deploy/press-agent/agent.yaml into the press routine at claude.ai/code/routines, preserving the <routine-fire-payload> opt-in (deploy/press-agent/README.md, 'post-merge re-paste'). Expect a burst right after any PR that changed that prompt merges — that is the detector working, not a bug.

panels.title: Agent CREDENTIAL redactions (24h) — expect 0 (#2508)
panels.description: sum by (op, reason) (increase(agent_reply_redacted_total{env="$env",channel="press"}[24h])) — each sample is a press agent that put a credential into text we were about to EMAIL to an untrusted, public journalist (or record on the public /press correspondence log). The AgentCredential redactor removed it before send, so nothing left the process; the sample means the agent TRIED — the higher-severity half of #2508, because the recipient sits outside every trust boundary. reason=agent_token means it quoted its own press session token; reason=bearer, any other credential-shaped value. Each is also logged at ERROR (the log never quotes the credential).

panels.title: Inbound dropped by the auto-reply/DSN loop guard, by reason (#2442)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(press_loop_guard_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — press mail the Cloudflare Email Worker (deploy/press-worker/src/loop-guard.ts) classified as machine-generated, so PressResponder dispatched NO agent session and sent NO reply. This is what stops a newsroom autoresponder from looping with us: prod's press From and Reply-To are both press@wifihaven.net (#2439), the address Email Routing binds to that same Worker, and the prod responder is live (#2537). reason=auto_submitted (RFC 3834 header, any value but `no`) / precedence (bulk|auto_reply|junk) / x_auto_response_suppress / list_id / null_return_path (a bounce/DSN, whose empty return path used to land in outcome=malformed) / unknown (a newer Worker sending a marker this API build does not know — still skipped, fail closed). A sustained rate is NOT automatically healthy: every sample is a press message we did not answer, so if it climbs, read the Worker's log line in Workers Logs (#2673) — it names the sender this counter deliberately does not — and confirm they were autoresponders rather than journalists.

panels.title: Press mail the loop guard did not answer (24h) (#2442)
panels.description: sum(increase(press_loop_guard_total{env="$env"}[24h])) — how many inbound press messages the loop guard declined in the last day. Zero is the steady state. A non-zero value is not itself a fault (one out-of-office is one sample), but it is the only counter that would move if a real journalist were misclassified as an autoresponder and never got a reply — cross-check against the Worker's log line, which carries the sender address.

title: WifiHaven — Press (PR)
